Three small business website packages, no surprises

Every small business website package here is a one-time price for a finished site you own. Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997. There is no deposit to get started, no contract, and no payment plan that quietly turns a website into a car note.

The difference between them is reach. Starter gives a single-town business five good pages. Pro adds the pages that help you get found in ten towns around you. Agency starts with keyword research across your whole service area and builds a page for every town-and-service combination the research says is worth having.

Before you choose, you can see a demo of your own site. Most people find the right package becomes obvious once they are looking at their business on their phone.

We do not sell page counts. Every page on every plan is researched and written by hand for your business and your town. That is slower than generating a few hundred pages from a template, and it is the reason these pages get read. If the research says your service area needs thirty pages, you get thirty good ones rather than a hundred thin ones.

Which package fits which business

A web design quote should start with how your customers find you, not with how many pages a designer wants to sell. Here is the honest version.

Starter fits

A business that mostly serves one town, or one that is brand new and needs a real website quickly. A barber in Big Sandy, a bookkeeper working from home, a food truck with a regular corner. Five pages, written well, are enough, and buying more would be waste.

Pro fits

A business whose customers come from several towns and describe the work in mostly the same words. A cleaning company covering a county, a salon that pulls clients from the next three towns over. Ten city pages put a real answer in front of each of those towns.

Agency fits

A business with several services across a wide area, where customers type genuinely different things: a remodeler, a law office with multiple practice areas, a clinic with a long list of treatments. Keyword research decides the page list first.

If you are stuck between two, take the smaller one. You can ask about more city pages later, once you see where calls come from, and the price is given before any work starts. And if you are unsure what your customers search for, read how city pages work before deciding.

Common questions

What comes in a small business website package?

The Starter package is a 5-page website (home, services, about, contact and service area), every page written by hand, built to work on phones, with a contact form, Google Maps and hours, links to Facebook and Instagram, and page titles, descriptions and a sitemap submitted to Google. Pro and Agency build on that. The comparison table on this page lists every item.

Can I get a web design quote for something that is not one of the packages?

Yes. Call or use the contact page and describe the job. Anything outside a package is quoted in writing before work starts, so you know the number first. Most local businesses fit one of the three packages, though, and the free demo is the fastest way to find out which.

Are these prices really one time, or is there a monthly fee?

The website itself is a one-time price: $497, $997 or $1,997. The monthly costs are separate and optional: the AI chat widget on Pro and the AI phone agent on Agency are $297 a month each after their free trials, and hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month if you do not keep an AI agent. While you keep the agent, hosting is included.

Is the AI phone agent included in the Agency price?

The setup is included. The agent itself is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, and you can cancel any time. It is not part of the one-time $1,997.

Do I have to pay before I see anything?

No. Ask for the free demo first. You see a site built for your business, and only then decide whether to buy a package. No deposit, no contract.

Which small business website package is the most popular?

Pro, at $997. It suits the common case of a business that serves more than one town: 10 pages, 10 researched city pages, schema markup and Google Business Profile setup.

See your site first, then pick a package

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
